response.design_spec:
# RV32I multicycle core with ready/valid memory interfaces

`luna_rv32` is based on the previously validated multi-cycle RV32I core and preserves its FETCH/DECODE/COMMIT sequencing, supported integer instruction behavior, trap behavior, and retirement fields. The instruction interface adds `imem_valid` and `imem_ready`: `imem_valid` is asserted only in FETCH while active, and instruction data plus PC are captured only on a cycle where `imem_ready` is high.

The data interface adds `dmem_ready`. A load or store keeps `dmem_valid` asserted in COMMIT until `dmem_ready` is high. Register writeback, PC update, and the single retirement event occur only on that completing handshake. Non-memory instructions commit without waiting for `dmem_ready`. `dmem_wstrb` and the effective address/data remain stable during the stalled COMMIT state because their source registers are not modified until the transaction completes.

The core remains RV32I integer-only and does not contain an FPU or floating-point ISA support. It is an integration primitive, not a complete TinyStories inference system. This RTL response has not been independently simulated, synthesized, placed/routed, programmed onto hardware, or used to run the model.
checks: Copied the existing rv32_multi core as baseline and renamed its module to luna_rv32.
Added imem_valid and imem_ready; FETCH captures instruction and PC only when imem_ready is asserted.
Added dmem_ready; load/store remain in COMMIT with dmem_valid asserted until ready, then perform their side effect, PC update, and one retirement pulse.
Preserved the baseline RV32I decode and trap logic; no floating-point ISA or FPU was added.
Static review only; no testbench, simulation, synthesis, FPGA programming, or physical-hardware verification performed.
